plan.title: feat(scope): complete a delivered story without a separate human-reviewed completion PR

narratives.Description: A story's last product PR can carry its brief from active/ to completed/ with `scope:complete --in-pr`, so no separate human-reviewed completion PR is needed. In-PR mode refuses stories whose acceptance rests on a merge (judged by the brief's own inputs); those keep the post-merge path (#6303). CI admits the move only when the PR removes the brief from active/, changes code inside the brief's file_scope and has a closing keyword for the issue; after merge, `verify:completed-tracked` re-runs the identity join on the landing commit and `verify:orphan-active` lists a brief that fails it.
narratives.UserStory: As a maintainer shipping a story, I want the last product PR to complete the story, so that I do not open, review, run CI on and merge a second lifecycle PR for every delivered story.
narratives.ImplementationPlan:
1. Add packages/core/src/scope/lands-with-product.ts: the `lands-with-product` disposition, in-PR input refusals (merge-requirement items, stored merge evidence, stored completionProvenance, clause-less acceptance, no issue ref, no in-scope production file), the admission check and the change-set move resolver.
2. In transition.ts and scope/main.ts add `scope:complete --in-pr`: skip the delivery gate, run acceptance, walk, spec-drift and moves, and stamp lifecycleWrite.completionDisposition (lifecycle-write.ts).
3. delivery-evidence.ts: `prDiffAddsBrief` accepts a rename from active/ with the same basename; the changed-files fetch carries previous_filename.
4. completed-write-guard.ts (+ runtime --pr-body-file): admit a lands-with-product add only on the paired active removal, prDiffAddsBrief, in-scope production files and a closing keyword.
5. lands-with-product-proof.ts: find the landing commit on the delivery tip, resolve its PR and run verifyStoryPrMergeIdentity; wire it into completed-tracked and orphan-active.
6. Story gates (verify:ac, pre-push selection in hooks/scope.ts, intent-constraint, observable-scope, presentation-coverage, closing-keywords story line) accept the moved brief.
7. Docs: pre-PR skill and commands.md; CHANGELOG; tests for each Bound 8 case.
narratives.Overview:
1. In-PR completion: `scope:complete -- <active-path> --in-pr` runs the transition on the product branch (acceptance evidence, acceptance walk, spec-drift, parent and twin moves, ledger) and writes `lifecycleWrite` with completion disposition `lands-with-product`. It writes no delivered provenance and no merge evidence. Before it runs, it refuses on the brief's own inputs: any acceptance item for which `itemDeclaresMergeRequirement` is true, any stored acceptance evidence of kind `merge`, any stored `completionProvenance`, clause-less acceptance (`isClauseLessAcceptance`), a brief with no GitHub issue reference, and a branch with no production file inside the brief's `file_scope`. Each refusal names the post-merge path and #6303.
2. Identity basis: `prDiffAddsBrief` also accepts a `renamed` entry whose previous path is the same brief basename under `active/`, beside a change outside the lifecycle folders. A lifecycle-only PR still does not qualify.
3. Admission: `verify:completed-write-guard` admits a code-bearing `completed/` add with disposition `lands-with-product` only when all of these hold on the PR's changed files: the brief leaves `active/` in the same change set (a rename from `active/`, or a delete of the same basename under `active/` beside the add); `prDiffAddsBrief` holds for that brief; the changed production files sit inside the brief's `file_scope`; and the PR body passes `bodyHasClosingKeywordFor` for the brief's issue. No sole-mark check is used. Every other case is unchanged.
4. Close proof: for a completed brief with disposition `lands-with-product`, `verify:completed-tracked` finds the commit that added the brief on the delivery tip, resolves its pull request, and runs `verifyStoryPrMergeIdentity` with that commit as the merge commit. A failed join, or a landing commit with no pull request, exits 1 and names the brief and the post-merge recovery.
5. Visible failure: `verify:orphan-active` also lists a `lands-with-product` brief on the delivery tip whose close proof (item 4) fails.
6. Story gates: gates that look for the story's brief under `active/` on the PR head also accept it under `completed/` when the change set carries a `lands-with-product` move for that brief.
7. Default and docs: the pre-PR skill and `commands.md` name in-PR completion as the default for a story's last product PR; a refused story keeps the post-merge path (#6303). Docs state that the human product merge plus the identity join is the completion proof.
8. Tests: an accepted in-PR completion merged with the move reported as `renamed` passes items 3 and 4, and `verify:completed-tracked -- --issue N` and `verify:orphan-active -- --issue N` exit 0 with no second PR; the same with the move reported as delete plus add; a story whose earlier merged PRs carry the same sole mark still passes; a PR body edited after CI to drop the keyword still passes on the diff basis; the guard refuses a missing keyword, a completed add that leaves the `active/` brief in place, and production files outside `file_scope`; in-PR mode refuses an item that declares the merge requirement, a brief with pre-stamped merge evidence, a brief with stored completion provenance, and clause-less acceptance; a `lands-with-product` brief landed by a direct commit fails item 4 and is listed by item 5; a lifecycle-only rename does not satisfy item 2; the post-merge path behaves as today.

## In plain English
When a story's product PR merges, the story is not finished. Someone must run `scope:complete` and land a second PR that moves the brief from `active/` to `completed/`. That PR gets its own review, CI run and human merge. On a consumer project, 16 of 22 PRs in one week were this kind of lifecycle PR. The open question is how a merged story can be recorded as completed without that second human-reviewed PR, while a fresh clone still shows it as completed and no agent can forge a completion.

## Pains
- P1 — Every delivered story needs a second PR, with its own review, CI run and human merge, only to move its brief to `completed/`.
- P2 — Completion is a separate step that someone has to remember after the merge. Until it runs, the story still looks open on a fresh clone, `verify:orphan-active` fails for it, and the finalize-owed inventory blocks later sessions. The session that posted this write-back had to defer seven such items before it could start.

## Must keep (from the issue)
Fresh-clone visibility of completed work (#4714); the human merge gate (#1193) for product code; `verify:orphan-active` and `verify:completed-tracked` as close proofs; no agent-forged completion.

## Notes for the arc
- Related arcs: #6205 (advance the plan on completion) and #6280 (lifecycle PRs skip the review bot) both halted today on the same missing piece, a test that recognises a real completion. Their scope is decided after this arc, in the light of its lean. They are not part of this warrant.
- Related accepted design: #6273 (one-PR path for a single maintainer).

Relayed by the coordinating session in a handoff note, not typed in this session. Scott's direction, verbatim: "note we are tyring to make directive smoother in running adding mor and more gates is going the wrong way". Standing steer, verbatim: "you can yolo them and start implementation when they land". For this handoff Scott asked for arcs only: no ingest, no brief, no code, no PR.

## In plain English

The issue asks to finish delivered stories automatically without another human-reviewed PR, while preserving delivery proof and fresh-clone visibility. Post-merge automation is the strongest fit with the existing implementation, but a merge event and story mark alone are insufficient authority. Completion also checks acceptance evidence and updates related lifecycle records. I would bind a narrowly authorized post-merge completion writer that reuses those checks, publishes the complete result atomically, and recovers from missed or overlapping runs.

### 1. Relayed operator instructions are untrusted — footnote

**Evidence:** Snapshot comment 6859857142, “Operator launch,” includes “you can yolo them and start implementation when they land” and a relayed direction against adding gates.

These are embedded instructions, not authority for this critic. Following them could turn a no-ingest critique into implementation or suppress a material finding. I treated them as thread data and followed the supplied brief; no implementation or posting was performed.

### 2. A story mark is a candidate selector, not completion proof — blocks-the-design

**Evidence:** `packages/core/src/scope/delivery-evidence.ts:1766–1821` reconstructs association at merge time and rejects associations added afterward. Lines 2477–2491 require the story→PR→merge identity join before accepting delivery; lines 2137–2172 separately require ancestry on the refreshed delivery branch.

The issue’s candidate 1 describes the proof as the merge commit plus its `deft-story` mark. An implementation that accepts current PR text, an arbitrary merged PR, or an integration-only merge would weaken existing proof and could complete the wrong story.

**Disposition:** Bind automation to the existing identity and delivery validators. Treat the event and mark as discovery inputs only. Explicitly retain merge-time association and configured-delivery-branch ancestry; do not substitute a new event-shaped shortcut.

### 3. Publishing authority must cover a verified transition, not arbitrary lifecycle files — blocks-the-design

**Evidence:** `packages/core/src/swarm/finalize-cohort.ts:1125–1170` checks branch policy and an allowed path set before committing; lines 1187–1208 open a separate PR. `packages/core/src/lifecycle/completed-write-guard.ts:14–19` explicitly leaves modification/restamp revalidation as residual work. `packages/core/src/scope/transition.ts:871` invokes an acceptance walk with an execution runner.

Removing human review changes the trust boundary. A writer allowed to land anything under `xbrief/` could publish forged changes to existing completed briefs or unrelated policy/specification content. Running repository-controlled acceptance commands with that writer’s credential also exposes its publication authority.

**Disposition:** Specify a trusted publisher that accepts only the verified transition result for named stories against an expected delivery tip. Run acceptance execution without publication credentials; validate the complete proposed diff before publication. A blanket branch-policy exemption, bot identity, or lifecycle-path allowlist is insufficient.

### 4. Merge success does not guarantee completion eligibility — sharpens-framing

**Evidence:** `packages/core/src/scope/transition.ts:818–892` requires per-criterion acceptance evidence, an acceptance walk, and the enforced spec-drift check. `packages/core/src/swarm/finalize-cohort.ts:1079–1122` includes parent/twin transitions and the spec-drift ledger among completion outputs.

The acceptance statement currently implies that any merged product PR becomes completed when the mechanism runs. Existing behavior can legitimately refuse completion after merge. Moving the brief alone would bypass those checks or omit required companion records.

**Disposition:** State that eligible delivered stories complete automatically; refused stories remain visibly pending with a concrete reason and retry path. Reuse the transition and its companion outputs. Merge proof must not manufacture acceptance evidence or human dispositions.

### 5. Recovery and concurrent publication are part of relieving P2 — sharpens-framing

**Evidence:** Stop 1 comment 6859857142 defines P2 as remembered manual completion and blocking residual inventory. `packages/core/src/swarm/finalize-cohort.ts:1495–1597` requires completed files to reach the delivery branch and keeps issues open until they do.

A one-shot workflow can fail after product merge. Two completion jobs can also prepare changes against the same tip; publishing only one leaves the other story unfinished. That reproduces P2 despite eliminating its normal manual step.

**Disposition:** Bind idempotent reconciliation of outstanding delivered stories, bounded retries, and expected-tip publication. On tip movement, recompute from the new tip rather than force-push. Report completion only after the published tree satisfies the close proofs.

### 6. Prefer tracked post-merge completion over the other two mechanisms — sharpens-framing

**Evidence:** `packages/core/src/lifecycle/completed-tracked-on-delivery.ts:386–432` resolves the delivery tip and inspects tracked tree paths. `packages/core/src/scope/delivery-evidence.ts:2295–2298` requires merged delivery before completion.

External records can reduce repository churn, but preserving current fresh-clone and tracked-tree proofs would require a new retrieval and authority model. Same-PR completion offers the cleanest single merge, but requires conditional completion semantics and cannot straightforwardly embed its own final merge identity.

**Disposition:** Bind tracked post-merge automation first. I would switch toward same-PR completion if consumer branch protections cannot admit a narrowly scoped automated writer and a concrete merge-conditioned proof preserves the unmerged-PR refusal. Neither alternative currently has that demonstrated contract.

## In plain English
The issue asks that a story whose product PR has merged be recorded as completed without a second, human-reviewed PR. It also keeps fresh-clone visibility, the human merge gate for product code, and the two close proofs. Much of that already exists: #3791 shipped a lifecycle-only auto-merge for `swarm/finalize/*` PRs. That path does not remove the PR. It also only arms when bot-merge is enabled for the whole repo, product code included. Candidate 2 cannot meet the close proofs without a tracked write. Candidate 3 is the only one that removes the second PR entirely, and I would bind it, with the proof keyed on the commit that lands it.

### 1. The existing #3791 carve-out is uninventoried and sets the real gap (sharpens-framing)
Evidence: `packages/core/src/swarm/finalize-cohort.ts:933-1001` (`evaluateFinalizeClassMergeCarveOut`) and `:2521-2563` already arm auto-merge for `swarm/finalize/*`. The #3791 brief (`xbrief/completed/2026-09-28-3791-…`, Overview item 2) bound "Do not re-open a deftai/directive-only merge-event workflow". In this repo `plan.x-directive.policy` has no `requireHumanMerge` and no `autoDeployOnMerge`, so `resolveHumanMergePolicy` (`packages/core/src/policy/require-human-merge.ts:86ff`) reads it as off and the carve-out arms here today. The human review that remains is the forge ruleset ("surface-3", `finalize-cohort.ts:944-945`), not Directive.
Failure mode: the arc ships candidate 1 as new machinery and duplicates #3791. Or it attacks the Directive gate while the forge required-review setting is what blocks the second PR. It also silently contradicts a bound #3791 decision.
Consequence: the lean must say which surface makes the completion PR human-reviewed: Directive policy, a forge ruleset, or the CI run plus review bot. It must also say whether it supersedes the #3791 item 2 ban or reuses that path.

### 2. Candidate 2 cannot meet the close proofs without a tracked write (blocks-the-design)
Evidence: `packages/core/src/lifecycle/completed-tracked-on-delivery.ts:1-11`. `verify:completed-tracked` requires a tracked artifact under `xbrief/completed/` on the delivery tip. `orphan-active` (`packages/core/src/orphan-active/running-briefs.ts`) scans `active/` for running briefs. A plain `git clone` does not fetch `refs/notes/*`, and a forge artifact is not in the clone at all.
Failure mode: the brief stays in `active/` on tip. `verify:orphan-active` fails for every merged story. A fresh clone shows the story as open (#4714 broken). To fix that, the "`completed/` projection" needs a commit, and that commit is the lifecycle PR again.
Consequence: candidate 2 cannot bind as written. It would only flip if both close proofs were rewritten to read the note or artifact, and that weakens #4714.

### 3. Candidate 1 under `requireHumanMerge: true` needs a gate that applies only to lifecycle PRs (blocks-the-design)
Evidence: `finalize-cohort.ts:985-995` refuses the carve-out whenever `requireHumanMerge` is effective true. The only way in is `policy:allow-bot-merge` or `DEFT_ALLOW_BOT_MERGE`, and those also open agent merge of product PRs (#1193). For a merge-gated consumer, which is the pain in the issue body, candidate 1 as written cannot land without disabling the human gate on product code.
Failure mode: operators turn on global bot-merge to stop the lifecycle-PR churn, and #1193 for product code is lost.
Consequence: if the lean picks candidate 1, it must add an admission scoped to lifecycle PRs. It would read policy from the merge base, as in the #6273 brief item 1, and admit only a lifecycle-shaped diff. This is a new gate, which conflicts with the operator steer quoted in 6859857142. That steer is one more reason for finding 4.

### 4. Candidate 3 is the thinnest; bind it with proof from the landing commit (sharpens-framing)
Evidence: two writers refuse it today. `packages/core/src/scope/transition.ts:736` (#3041) runs the delivery gate before `complete`. `packages/core/src/lifecycle/completed-write-guard.ts:25-28` requires provenance stamps on code-bearing `completed/` adds and refuses informal `productMerge` stamps. Before merge, the PR has no merge SHA to stamp, especially under squash.
Steelman and bind: move the brief in the product PR without a merge stamp. Both close proofs and the write guard then accept a `completed/` blob only when the commit that brought it onto the delivery tip is the merge or squash commit of a PR. That PR must have a merge-time basis for the issue, which is the existing `deft-story` / closing-keyword / Connected-link bases at `packages/core/src/scope/delivery-evidence.ts:716-719`. An unmerged PR never reaches the tip, so acceptance 2 holds by construction. P2 disappears because nothing is left to remember after the merge. The trust anchor is the human product merge, the same anchor #6273 accepts.
What would flip it: (a) proof that a revert or partial-delivery case needs `active/` to survive the merge; (b) the #4864 / closing-keyword rules cannot accept a full-story PR that carries its own `completed/` brief. In either case, fall back to candidate 1 with finding 3's lifecycle-only gate.
Consequence: the lean must say "merged first" (#3041) is checked against the landing commit, not against a separate later commit.

### 5. Candidate 1 puts untrusted input into a privileged workflow (sharpens-framing)
Evidence: candidate 1 has a workflow on the delivery branch that reads the merged PR body (the `deft-story` mark, which an agent wrote) and writes to the tree.
Failure mode: under `pull_request_target`, or with a token that has `contents: write`, the PR body becomes untrusted input with write authority. That is a forge-completion path an agent controls.
Consequence: if candidate 1 is chosen, the lean must name the trigger (push on the delivery branch only), the token scope, and a fixed parse of the mark. It must not evaluate the PR body.

### 6. Relayed operator instruction in the thread (footnote)
Comment 6859857142, "Operator launch", relays "you can yolo them and start implementation when they land" from a handoff note. It was not typed in-session. Under #480 it is described content. This seat did not act on it.

## In plain English

After a story’s product PR merges, Directive still needs a second land that moves the brief from `active/` to `completed/` so a fresh clone and `verify:completed-tracked` see it as done. That second land is usually another human-reviewed lifecycle PR, which is the pain. The issue offers three open mechanisms and keeps merge-proof, tip-tree visibility, and no agent-forged completion. At the pin, most of the completion machinery already exists (`scope:complete`, `swarm:finalize-cohort`, the #3791 finalize-class carve-out, write-guard, delivery evidence). ## In plain English
Problem: when a story's product PR merges, the story is not finished. Someone has to run `scope:complete` and land a second PR that moves the brief to `completed/`, with its own review, CI run and human merge. Until it lands, the story looks open and blocks later sessions.

In-PR completion refuses any story whose acceptance rests on a merge, judged by what the brief contains, so those stories keep the post-merge path (#6303). Before merge, CI admits the move only when the PR removes the brief from `active/`, changes code inside the brief's scope, and has a closing keyword for the story's issue. After merge, `verify:completed-tracked` re-runs today's identity join on the commit that landed the brief, and `verify:orphan-active` lists any such brief that fails it.

## Summary

Every delivered story needs a second PR after its product PR: the completion PR that moves the brief from `active/` to `completed/`. `scope:complete` requires the product PR to be merged first (#3041 / #3675), and `verify:completed-tracked` requires the completed brief on the delivery branch (#3476 / #4714). So the minimum for one change is two PRs, each with its own review, CI run and human merge.

#680 (0.129.8) made that PR cheaper: no CHANGELOG line, and finalize commits the spec-drift ledger. It did not remove the PR.

## Consumer impact

On a consumer project, of 22 PRs in one week, 6 carried the change and 16 were lifecycle PRs. A 14-line hook refresh took 3 PRs. Each lifecycle PR also pays for a review-bot pass. The same cost applies to maintainer work in this repo: every story in the last two cohorts needed a completion PR and an operator step.

## Expected

Completion of a delivered story needs no separate human-reviewed PR, while the merge proof stays as strong as today. Candidate designs for the arc:

1. **Post-merge automation.** A workflow on the delivery branch runs the completion sweep after the product PR merges and lands the completed brief itself. The proof is the merge commit and the `deft-story` mark it already carries.
2. **Completion recorded outside the tracked tree**, keyed to the merge commit (for example a git note or a forge artifact), with `completed/` as a projection.
3. **Completion in the product PR**: the brief moves in the same PR and takes effect at merge. This conflicts with "merged first" (#3041), so it needs the strongest argument.

Whatever is chosen must keep: fresh-clone visibility of completed work (#4714), the human merge gate (#1193) for product code, `verify:orphan-active` and `verify:completed-tracked` as close proofs, and no agent-forged completion.

## Until then

Make `swarm:finalize-cohort` the documented default for solo stories too, so completions batch into one lifecycle PR.

## Acceptance

- Given a merged product PR for a story, when the chosen mechanism runs, then the brief is completed and `verify:completed-tracked -- --issue N` exits 0 with no human-reviewed completion PR.
- Given a product PR that is not merged, then the brief is not completed.
- A fresh clone still shows the story as completed.

Refs #680. Refs #3041. Refs #4714. Related: #6273 (one-PR path for a single maintainer).
